newsitem.title: USA: Great Western, Wash. Mutual holders OK deal.
newsitem.headline: Great Western, Wash. Mutual holders OK deal.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp. and Washington Mutual Inc. shareholders Friday approved a $6.9 billion merger of the two companies that will create the nation's largest savings and loan -- but at the cost of thousands of jobs.

At a special meeting in Chatsworth, Calif., shareholders representing 98 percent of Great Western's voting shares approved the deal. Washington Mutual shareholders also voted to approve the deal at a separate meeting in Seattle, where that thrift is based.
The shareholder vote came a little more than a week after H.F. Ahmanson and Co. dropped its hostile bid for Great Western, ending a bitter savings-and-loan takeover battle.
Chatsworth-based Great Western, which has cut its work force by 30 percent since 1993, now employs about 12,000 people.

Industry and company sources have estimated 2,000 to 3,000 jobs will be cut due to the merger, with many occurring at the thrift's Chatsworth headquarters, where the company employs about 2,800 people.
"How will the deal benefit the Southern California community other than putting a few bucks in the shareholders' pockets?" asked one shareholder at the meeting.

Great Western Chief Executive John Maher, who will leave his post once the deal is done, said the merged company, which will have have assets of $86 billion, will generate signficant benefits to customers, communities and employees.

"There will be some job losses. Approximately 100 branches in California will be consolidated, but the job loss will be significantly less than with the proposed Ahmanson deal," said Maher, who will receive about $10 million when he leaves his post within weeks once the merger is completed.
Analysts had estimated a merger of Irwindale, Calif.-based Ahmanson and Great Western would have eliminated 4,500 to 6,000 positions.

"As far as the actual number of individuals (to be eliminated, I don't have a number. I think plans from Washington Mutual will be forthcoming in the next three to four weeks," Maher told reporters after the meeting.
"I think the order of magnitude of branch closings with Ahmanson was double," said Maher.

"There won't be much middle management left," said one executive. "I suspect a lot of people who earn salaries north of $100,000 will start to get notices next week, and there are a lot of people like that."

Ahmanson launched its offer in February. Great Western rejected the bid and on March 6 announced it agreed to be bought by Washington Mutual. After trying unsuccessfully to persuade shareholders to support its bid, Ahmanson withdrew its offer June 4.

Several analysts have said that Ahmanson's defeat in the takeover battle leaves the thrift as a vulnerable takeover target. They said Washington Mutual may try to buy Ahmanson once its integration with Great Western is completed.
Maher said he believed Washington Mutual will want to further boost its presence in Florida after the Great Western deal, which will add 120 Florida Great Western locations.
"I know there's an attitude and appetite but will not comment beyond that," said Maher when asked if further acquisitions there were being considered.
